title: Ordinary call: church election by pastors, magistrate, people; requisites
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Paul teaches ye requisites (1 Tim. 3; Tit. 1): common—faithful, blameless, sober, hospitable, just; proper toward ye office—apt toward teach, holding sound doctrine, able toward exhort and refute opponents, not neophytes. — Ye means belonging toward ordinary calling stands as ye Church's lawful election. God gave His church ye keys belonging toward ye kingdom and entrusted word and sacraments; therefore ye church elects ministers through three orders: ye eldership or pastors; magistrates as nursing fathers; and ye Christian people.
pass_b_english: The means of ordinary calling is the Church's lawful election. God gave His church the keys of the kingdom and entrusted word and sacraments; therefore the church elects ministers through three orders: the eldership or pastors; magistrates as nursing fathers; and the Christian people.

Paul teaches the requisites (1 Tim. 3; Tit. 1): common—faithful, blameless, sober, hospitable, just; proper to the office—apt to teach, holding sound doctrine, able to exhort and refute opponents, not neophytes.
source_text: Medium vocationis ordinariae est electio Ecclesiae legitima. Deus ecclesiae suae dedit claves regni caelorum (Matt. 16:18; 18:17) verbumque et sacramenta concredidit. Quapropter ecclesia Dei eligit et vocat ministros per tres ordines: (1) presbyterii sive pastorum ecclesiae (Acts 14:23; 1 Tim. 4:14; Tit. 1:5); (2) magistratuum, qui sunt membra ecclesiae et nutritii (Isa. 49:23); (3) populi Christiani (Acts 6:3; 14:23; 1 Cor. 16:3). Quales personae eligendae sint docet Paulus (1 Tim. 3; Tit. 1): communia—fideles, irreprehensibiles, sobrii, hospitales, iusti; propria—apti ad docendum, tenaces sanae doctrinae, potentes exhortari et contradicentes refellere, non neophyti.
